newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone soldiers in court on treason charges.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone soldiers in court on treason charges.

text.p: Nine soldiers have appeared in court in Sierra Leone on charges of trying to topple the elected civilian government in September, court sources said.
The nine, including a woman who heard about the coup but failed to pass on details to the authorities, have all been charged with treason and face execution if found guilty.
The court, in a preliminary hearing late on Tuesday, did not take pleas and remanded the accused in custody until December 19.
The charge sheet accused them of plotting to ambush President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah's convoy on his way to work and detain him.
It also said that they had plotted to arrest senior military officers in Freetown to prevent them foiling the coup attempt.
Tejan Kabbah took power in March after winning multi-party elections called to end four years of army rule. His government and rebels signed a peace deal in Ivory Coast on November 30.
